title: Isolate kernel dependency contracts, shrink runtime images, and add compatibility regression harness
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: The runtime image bundles multiple GPU dependency entrypoints and transitive libraries (CUTLASS, Triton plugins, vendor kernels). This causes large image sizes, unclear compatibility boundaries, and frequent rollbacks during CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS upgrades. Cold-start latency spikes are observed when the runtime probes and links a chain of optional plugins; our current probe/shim approach increases OOM risk in constrained Dedicated nodes.

Goal: Reduce image footprint and probe jitter, make kernel dependency contracts explicit, and add a CI-driven compatibility regression harness so future dependency bumps are gated by reproducible performance/functional tests.

Scope:
- Introduce a minimal "core runtime" package that contains only absolute runtime essentials and a clearly versioned kernel-deps contract file.
- Split optional GPU plugin bundles (cutlass variants, triton-plugins, quant-kernels) to separate artifacts that are dynamically loaded by the core runtime via a small, audited loader.
- Add deterministic prelinking and symbol quarantine step in the build pipeline to catch symbol collisions early.
- Implement a regression harness: matrix CI that builds small reproducer images across targeted CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS combinations and runs latency/throughput microbenchmarks plus basic functional smoke tests.
- Gather and surface telemetry for kernel selection and probe durations to the Console to verify cold-start improvements.

Proposed implementation:
1) Design a kernel-deps contract file format (JSON) with explicit ABI, expected symbols, and a capability tag. The loader validates this contract before attempting dlopen.
2) Move vendor-optional artifacts into separate packages (runtime-core, runtime-plugins-{cutlass, triton, quant}).
3) Add a lightweight loader with a safe sandbox mode: try dlopen, if failure mark plugin as incompatible and fall back without bringing down the runtime.
4) Add a build-time prelink stage that runs in CI using a hermetic container to detect missing symbols/collisions and produce a human-readable report.
5) Extend CI (canary-matrix) to run the reproducible harness across a curated set of CUDA (11.8, 12.2, 12.4) x Triton (2.x, 3.x) x CUTLASS (1.x, 2.x) combos. Fail PRs that introduce regressions beyond threshold.

Tradeoffs and risks:
- Extra packaging complexity and release steps. We mitigate with a simple release script that still publishes a combined artifact for convenience.
- Slight runtime cost for loader validation on cold start; expected to be <6ms and offset by overall reduced probe jitter.
- CI matrix increase in runtime; mitigate by running full matrix only on release branches and a minimal smoke-check on PRs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Core runtime image size reduced by at least 18% compared to baseline (measured on our docker base image). 
- Median cold-start probe time reduced by >=25% in dedicated-node repros.
- CI matrix detects a seeded incompatibility (test seed PR linked below) and blocks the merge.
- Documentation: Confluence design doc and release checklist updated.

Follow-ups (after merge):
- Roll out dynamic plugin loading to a subset of Dedicated pools as a canary.
- Add telemetry-based automated fallback policies if a plugin starts failing in production.
